Composer

The prompt input under a transcript: a textarea that grows with its content, and Send.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • At the bottom of a transcript, to send the next prompt to the agent.
  • To stop a running turn from the same place the reader sends from.

When not to use it

  • For one line of text in a form, such as a task title. Use a field.
  • For longer text that is saved with a form and not sent as a message. Use a textarea.
  • To answer an approval request. Use the approval's own Allow and Decline.

Variants

default
In the flow of the page, as wide as its container.
sticky ds-composer--sticky
Held to the bottom of the scrolling view, with a top border, its own padding and room for the home indicator. Make the view's scroller end at the visible viewport, with a height in dvh or interactive-widget=resizes-content in the viewport meta tag, so it stays above an on-screen keyboard.

Sizes

default
The textarea is one line and 44px tall when empty and grows with its content to 176px, then scrolls. Where field-sizing is not supported it is a fixed 88px. Send stays beside the last line.

Accessibility

  • Use a form element, so Send submits it. The textarea has a visible ds-composer__label whose for attribute matches its id, or an aria-label when the view has no room for one. A placeholder is not a label.
  • Send is a button of type submit with ds-button ds-button--primary. It is the view's one primary action, so nothing else in the view is primary.
  • While a turn runs, the app sets aria-busy="true" on the form and replaces Send with a Stop button of type button and secondary emphasis. Never show both. The textarea stays editable, and a line of ds-composer__reason linked by aria-describedby says when sending is possible again.
  • When the reader cannot send, set disabled on the textarea and on Send, and say why in ds-composer__reason, linked from both by aria-describedby. The reason says what to do next.
  • When a prompt fails to send, keep the text in the textarea and add ds-composer__error with role="alert", linked by aria-describedby. Its icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
  • Tab moves from the textarea to Send, then to the quiet controls. The app decides whether Enter sends. If it does, Shift+Enter adds a line, and the button remains the way to send on a phone.
  • The component needs no script. The app sets disabled, aria-busy and aria-describedby, and swaps Send for Stop.
